subject: POC Success Criteria & Evaluation Plan — Redwood Inference POC
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@acme-retail.com>; Michael Chen <mchen@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Recap & POC plan — next steps and success criteria

Hi Aisha / Michael —

Thanks for the time today — great conversation and excited about the potential to help Acme speed up search personalization on mobile. Below is a short recap from our discovery and a proposed POC/eval plan so we can align on success criteria, timeline, ownership, and next steps.

Recap (key needs)
- Primary goal: improve relevance of product recommendations in search while meeting mobile latency SLOs and controlling per-request cost.
- Typical traffic: 120 RPS peak on search endpoints (mobile), average query length ~18 tokens.
- Data availability: anonymized sample of 10k production queries + top 100k product embeddings available for POC.

Proposed POC scope (2-week focused trial)
- Objectives: Validate latency & throughput with 95th percentile latency <= 200 ms for <512 token context; evaluate quality uplift vs baseline model; measure cost/token and per-request unit economics.
- Evaluation dataset: 5k holdout queries (provided by Acme) + 2 synthetic edge-case sets we’ll generate for long queries and multi-turn clarifications.
- Success criteria (draft):
  - Latency: 95th percentile <= 200 ms (p95) under production-like concurrency (simulated 80% of peak = 96 RPS)
  - Throughput: sustain 100 RPS with average response time < 120 ms for common 1–2 token completions
  - Cost: target inference cost <= $0.0007 per token (we’ll report cost/token for different configs)
  - Quality: improve top-5 recommendation hit-rate by >= 8% over current model OR human-eval pass-rate >= 85% on prioritized prompt sets
- Instrumentation: we’ll provide a test harness for replaying requests and measuring latency/cost; need a small API endpoint from Acme for replay (read-only, sample data) and an initial set of golden prompts.

Ownership & contacts
- Redwood: Jordan (sales/POC lead) — jordan_blake@redwood.ai; Sean (solutions engineer) — sean_gallagher@redwood.ai; Marissa (customer success) — marissa_cole@redwood.ai
- Acme: Aisha (product) — aisha@acme-retail.com; Michael (infra/prod) — mchen@acme-retail.com

Timeline & next steps
1) Confirm success criteria above (reply with any edits) — by Thu 22 Jan
2) Exchange trial agreement & schedule kickoff — target kickoff Mon 2 Feb
3) Provide sample dataset + test endpoint details — by Mon 26 Jan
4) Redwood to share detailed POC plan + timeline doc (attached) — by Wed 21 Jan

Attachments: acme-poc-plan.xlsx (POC tasks & ownership), redwood-poc-timeline.pdf (timeline draft)

Do you want to adjust the latency target or evaluation windows? Happy to make this conservative or aggressive depending on what matters most to you.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
(415) 555-0123
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@acme-retail.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Chen <mchen@acme-retail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jan 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap & POC plan — next steps and success criteria

Thanks Jordan — really helpful recap. A few quick notes from our side:

1) Latency target — our internal goal for mobile is tighter; can we aim for p95 <= 150 ms for the mobile search path? If that’s not feasible during initial test, we can accept p95 <= 200 ms but would prefer to see a plan for reaching 150 ms within a quarter.
2) Quality metrics — the top-5 hit-rate improvement goal looks good; for human evals we’d like to use a small panel (5 PMs/merchandisers) instead of a single annotator. Can Redwood support that flow?
3) Instrumentation & data handling — we can provide a read-only replay endpoint and the 5k holdout by Mon 26 Jan. We do need clarity on where logs/metrics will live (Redwood console or pushed back to our Datadog). Also, any SOC2 / data handling docs would be useful for our security team.

Assuming we can get the SOC2 summary and a simple metrics export (Prometheus/Datadog), we’re good to proceed. Also can we add a short milestone for model/regression monitoring after the POC (one-week stabilization window)?

Happy to hop on a quick 20-min sync if useful.

—Aisha
Product Manager, Acme Retail
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@acme-retail.com>, Michael Chen <mchen@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Jan 2026 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap & POC plan — next steps and success criteria

Great — thanks for the quick feedback, Aisha. Responses inline: 

1) Latency: We can start with p95 <= 200 ms as a conservative baseline during the first week of the POC and run an optimization sprint (kernel selection, batching, quantization profiles) in week 2 to target p95 <= 150 ms. We’ll capture telemetry for both p50/p95/p99 and provide recommendations and expected lift timeline.

2) Human eval panel: Yes — Redwood can coordinate a small panel and produce a simple UI for annotators. Marissa will own the logistics for the annotator workflow and consolidation of results.

3) Instrumentation & data handling: We can push metrics to your Datadog via our metric exporter and also show them in Redwood Console. I’ve attached a SOC2-summary.pdf for your security team. We will not persist PII and will use the anonymized dataset you provide.

4) Regression monitoring milestone: agreed — we’ll include a one-week stabilization window post-POC for monitoring and minor tuning.

Next steps (updated)
- Jordan to send trial agreement & kickoff calendar invite — by EOD Thu 22 Jan
- Acme to provide 5k holdout dataset + replay endpoint details — by Mon 26 Jan
- Redwood to prepare annotator workflow and tagging guidelines — Marissa to send by Tue 27 Jan

Marissa — can you take point on the annotator flow and the human-eval schedule? Sean — please draft the test harness plan and load profile we’ll use for the replay.

Thanks — looking forward to kickoff.

Jordan
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@acme-retail.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Michael Chen <mchen@acme-retail.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Jan 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap & POC plan — next steps and success criteria

Thanks team — I’ll own the human-eval panel and the acceptance criteria documentation. Quick notes: 

- Acceptance criteria (final checklist we’ll use):
  1) p95 latency <= 200 ms for week 1 load; target p95 <= 150 ms by end of week 2 (optimization track)
  2) Sustained throughput >= 100 RPS during replay with <5% error rate
  3) Cost per token reported and baseline comparison included; no strict hard limit besides the draft target — we’ll provide a cost-sensitivity table
  4) Human-eval: >=85% pass-rate across the Acme panel OR top-5 hit-rate lift >=8%
  5) No data exfiltration or storage of raw PII; confirm anonymization step before dataset handoff

- I’ve attached the preliminary acceptance checklist and a short schedule for the annotator sessions.
- Michael — when you share the replay endpoint, please include any auth details and rate limits. If you want, Marissa and I can run a short connectivity test next Tue.

Next actions: trial agreement signature, dataset handoff, and kickoff slide + calendar.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success
Redwood Inference
